summary: Spanish Austen criticism and two distinct French Kafka interpretations add form-specific comparisons. A Brazilian Woolf abstract supplies a narrowly labelled interpretive lead; full text was unavailable.
next: Strengthen Mrs Dalloway beyond abstract evidence; consult new science/history candidates and substantive reader discussions.

sources.title: Orgullo y prejuicio: El número 1 de Austen
sources.author: Lucía Martínez Alcalde
sources.note: Locates achievement in free indirect discourse, irony and moral self-correction, connecting marriage conventions and inherited privilege with the novel’s comic force.
sources.limits: One critic’s appraisal; title is an Austen-specific preference, not a global numerical ranking.

sources.title: Franz Kafka, ou l’aveu de la réalité
sources.publisher: Les Personnes du drame; digital edition Université de Genève
sources.author: Denis de Rougemont
sources.note: Reads The Trial through exact everyday observation and suspended judgment, and The Castle through uncertain grace; its explicit Christian framework exposes interpretive commitments.
sources.limits: 1944 theological interpretation, not neutral explanation of authorial intention; references to Brod are dependent, not separately consulted.

sources.title: Pour un Kafka en procès
sources.author: Gerhard Neumann; French translation Isabelle Vodoz
sources.note: Opening argues that Kafka transforms narrative formation into a process of writing, with The Trial joining discipline, freedom, interrogation and comedy.
sources.limits: Only accessible opening examined, not the complete pages 63–87. Supports this stated thesis without claiming its full demonstration.

sources.title: O sotão de Virgina Woolf: um diálogo com a loucura feminina?
sources.author: Allana Meneses
sources.note: Abstract proposes that fragmented time and interior narration make Mrs Dalloway a critique of patriarchal regulation and normalized psychological experience.
sources.limits: Full PDF unavailable. Records the stated interpretation only; no claim to have evaluated its textual argument or clinical validity.
